CORAM:
HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE MINI PUSHKARNA ORDER % 17.02.2023 [Physical Hearing/ Hybrid Hearing]
1.

The present writ petitions have been filed with prayer for directions to the respondents to pay Special Rehabilitation Package to the petitioners in the same manner and on the same terms as has been paid to similarly situated villagers of Villages Pooth Khurd, Sultanpur, Karala and Kanjhawala, whose land has also been acquired at the same time when the land of the Petitioners has been acquired.
2. It is the case of the petitioners that they are the co-sharers of the land of various Khasra numbers, situated in Revenue Estate of Village Tikri Khud, Delhi.
3. A Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued showing intention to acquire the land of the various Khasra numbers of the village in question.
The Declaration under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued on 22.02.2007.
This was followed by Award dated 16.02.2009 bearing Award No.10 of 2008-09/DC/NW of Village Tikri Khurd.

4. It is the case of the petitioner that a Writ Petition being W.P.(C) No. 537/2010 was filed before this Court for seeking payment of compensation amount and also the amount of Special Rehabilitation Package.
However, no payment for Special Rehabilitation Package was made.

Thus, it is submitted that by judgment dated 27.09.2011 in W.P.(C) No. 537/2010, directions were given by this Court to the Revenue Authorities to offer payment of Special Rehabilitation Package to the various persons who were inhabitants of the village in question, in terms of the office order dated 01.10.2008 of the respondents.

5. It is submitted that since the judgment dated 27.09.2011 passed by this Court in W.P.(C) No. 537/2010 was not complied with, a Contempt petition being Contempt Case (Civil) No. 929/2011 titled as 'Ashwani Kumar Vs. Lal Singh and Another' and Contempt Case (Civil) No.201/2012 titled as "Rohtas Vs. Vijay Dev & Another"
came to be filed.

entities.text: Ashwani Kumar Vs. Lal Singh and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the said Contempt Cases came to be disposed of with liberty to raise claims with respect to the difference of amounts payable to the petitioners herein.

10 6.
It is submitted that Writ Petition (Civil) No. 8823/2017 was disposed of by this Court by judgment dated 18.08.2022.

By the said judgment, co-ordinate Bench of this Court had allowed the writ petitions, thereby directing the Authorities to make the payment of Special Rehabilitation Package in the same manner as has been made qua other aforesaid villages.

It is further submitted that this Court in the said judgment dated 18.08.2022 in W.P.(C) No. 8823/2017 has recorded a definite finding that there is discrimination qua village in question i.e. Village Tikri Khurd with regard to the calculation, which has been made qua other four villages, namely, Pooth Khurd,
Sultanpur, Karala and Kanjhawala.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that a similar Writ Petition being W.P.(C) No.
1136/2023 was filed, in which notice has already been issued and the same is pending consideration before this Court on 29.05.2023.
8. In view thereof, issue notice to the respondent.

CORAM:
HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE MINI PUSHKARNA ORDER % 17.02.2023
[Physical Hearing/ Hybrid Hearing]

1. The present writ petition has been filed with prayer for directions to the respondent No. 2 i.e. Revenue Assistant/ SDM Kanjawala to dispose of the corrigendum/rectification application dated 11.02.2022 filed vide diary No.2084.

The said application has been filed by the petitioner with prayer for rectification of the final order dated 24.01.2022 in terms of the order as passed on 12.03.2021 in case no.
274/RA/SDM/SV/1997.
2.
It is the case on behalf of the petitioner that land in question was purchased by father-in-law of the petitioner.

Subsequently, the patwari concerned made a report dated 10.02.1994 with respect to violation of Section 81 of Delhi Land Reforms (DLR)
Act, 1954 in regard to Khasra No. 351 Min (0-15) & 352 Min (0-09).
Show cause notice was issued to the recorded owner i.e. Sh. Kimti Lal Jain on 03.10.1994.

It is submitted that the conditional order dated 08.09.1997 was passed by the court of SDM (Saraswati Vihar) in Case No. 274/RA/SV/97 after taking actual spot inspection report from the Halka Patwari report dated 12.02.1997.
3.

It is the case of the petitioner that the recorded owner i.e. Sh.
Kimti Lal Jain executed Gift Deed after taking NOC in favour of his daughter- in-law i.e. Smt. Nisha Jain, the petitioner herein.
4. It is submitted that the concerned Patwari submitted the field inspection report with photographs clearly stating that the Khasra No.351 min (0-15) & 352 min (0-09) was vacant land.
The petitioner installed electricity connection in her name on 14.08.2020.
Subsequently, SDM submitted a spot inspection report dated 09.12.2020 along with sizra/ map of the field in question.

The petitioner filed her detailed reply on 18.01.2021 and the matter was fixed for final arguments on 12.03.2021.
5.
It is submitted that vide order dated 12.03.2021, the concerned SDM pronounced the judgment.
Thus, by order dated 12.03.2021, it was recorded that Khasra No. 351 to the extent it is built up with farm house as per Halka Patwari report, is vested in Gram Sabha.

Thus, the proceedings were dropped vide order dated 12.03.2021 passed by the SDM.
6.

It is the case of the petitioner that the SDM passed a detailed order subsequently on 24.01.2022,
whereby it was stated that the land of the petitioner of Khasra No. 351 (0-15) was vested in Gram Sabha, Sawda contrary to the order of pronouncement dated 12.03.2021.
7.

Thus, noting the aforesaid discrepancy, the petitioner moved a corrigendum/rectification application dated 11.02.2022, thereby requesting the SDM to rectify the judgement dated Ritu vs Kamla Devi on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17345247/
12 24.01.2022 in terms of what was reflected in the order sheet dated 12.03.2021.
8.
It is the case on behalf of the petitioner that till date, the said application of the petitioner is pending disposal despite many personal visits by the petitioner as well as her Advocate.
The concerned SDM has not taken any action.
9. Issue notice.
10. Notice is accepted by learned counsel appearing for all the respondents.
Learned counsel submits that the application of the petitioner shall be dealt with on merits expeditiously and in accordance with law.

11. In that view of the matter, the present writ petition is disposed of with directions to the respondents to decide the application of the petitioner at the earliest preferably within three months from today.
Further, the petitioner is also given liberty to file any other additional documents or any other fresh application in this regard.
12. In case the petitioner is aggrieved by any order that may be passed by the concerned SDM, the petitioner is at liberty to seek remedy, as per law.
13. Needless to say, this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case.
14. Petition is disposed of in terms of the aforesaid.
